extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community: investigators, institution research administrators, and applicants for NIH funding
extracted.subtask_description: A news/index page summarizing recent NIH extramural policy updates, resources, and reminders that affect grant applicants and awardees. It highlights topics investigators should note when preparing applications or managing awards (e.g., data management formats, replication expectations, review-process changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting appropriate research models (New Approach Methodologies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions when using New Approach Methodologies (NAMs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance understanding of human health and disease, and while encouraging methods that enhance human relevance and translational potential, investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: A new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format is available based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants preparing DMS Plans for applicable submissions should use the 2026 pilot format and its simplified required elements; see the new resource for specifics (announcement dated April 29, 2026).

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed replication and reproducibility throughout NIH-supported research
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants and awardees should incorporate replication and reproducibility practices across applications and awards as part of NIH's effort to ensure research reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH's Gold Standard Science plan advances a commitment to replication and reproducibility, and the new Replication and Reproducibility Initiative is intended to drive, incentivize, and institutionalize replication and reproducibility efforts across the biomedical research enterprise. This is positioned as a 'highlighted topic' applicants should consider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand PF5 (Collaborative International Research Projects) application format and award structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Prospective applicants should learn key features of the new PF5 award structure, the application format, and that applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time (JIT) requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH published a 6-minute video overview describing PF5's award structure and how applications may be handled (e.g., potential splitting into linked awards post-review and prior to JIT). Applicants should watch to learn format and structural implications for submission and funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of 'Competitive But Not Discussed' review designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Following emergency review modifications, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed' recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cutoff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This designation affects which applications are discussed at study section meetings; applicants receiving this score were considered in the middle third of applications and therefore not discussed despite being competitive. The change followed emergency modifications after a lapse in appropriations (context: implemented last November).

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized peer review within CSR (impacts on efficiency, competition, transparency)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH centralized all peer review within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) to strengthen efficiency, competition, and transparency in the peer-review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As of March 2025 consolidation of peer review into CSR is intended to affect review operations and processes; applicants and reviewers should be aware of organizational/operational changes and their initial effects on peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor NIH schedules, program re-openings, and policy announcements (operational reminders)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators and administrators should monitor NIH announcements for practical operational items—e.g., upcoming National Advisory Council/Board meetings, office closures, and program status changes (such as the NIH Seed Fund returning).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists calendar items and program updates (e.g., NIH closed on May 25, 2026; NIH Seed Fund/Small Business Program returning) that can affect submission timing, institutional planning, and awareness of funding opportunities.
